articles.title: Deloitte Canada cuts GDP forecast by 20% as tariffs grip economy amid Trump's trade war
articles.summary: Deloitte Canada has shaved 20 per cent off its growth forecast for Canada's economy in 2027, citing increasingly tough conditions for consumers and businesses. The accounting firm's latest outlook…

image.caption: Workers are pictured at Amazon's 825,000-square-foot fulfilment and distribution centre in Pitt Meadows, B.C, on June 6, 2025. (Ben Nelms/CBC)

blocks.text: Business·New

Deloitte Canada has shaved 20 per cent off its growth forecast for Canada's economy in 2027, citing increasingly tough conditions for consumers and businesses. The accounting firm's latest outlook comes as a new American ban on select Canadian imports took effect.
Fallout of recent trade escalations likely to cause sharp economic slowdown in Q4 and early 2027, firm says
Deloitte Canada has shaved 20 per cent off its growth forecast for Canada's economy in 2027, citing increasingly tough conditions for consumers and businesses.
The accounting firm's latest outlook comes as a new American ban on select Canadian imports took effect on Tuesday.
Deloitte sees the fallout of recent escalations in the Canada-U.S. trade war causing a sharp economic slowdown in the final quarter of this year and into early 2027.

Chief economist Dawn Desjardins says the weight of billions of dollars in U.S. tariffs and Canada's reciprocal measures will not fall evenly across the Canadian economy, hitting some sectors hard, while others prosper. At the same time, the federal government's fiscal supports, investment initiatives and defence spending are positive signals for targeted growth, she said.

"For some, it's a little bit like the Earth is moving under their feet — and not in a positive way. While in other sectors, I think we can anticipate growth and job creation," Desjardins told CBC News in an interview prior to the report's release on Tuesday.

items: Canada's economy has found its footing. But is it enough to survive the U.S. trade war?

blocks.text: Deloitte's latest economic outlook for Canada calls for GDP to grow 1.6 per cent in 2027. In late June, the firm said it expected two per cent GDP growth next year.
Deloitte currently sees Canada's economy growing by 0.9 per cent in 2026 — a slight improvement from its June estimate of 0.7 per cent.

"It's so uncertain when we think about all the factors the Canadian companies are facing, whether it's the prospect of higher costs, the prospect of more friction with our largest trading partner or perhaps even higher interest rates. All these factors are just creating a very uncertain environment," Desjardins said.
"As a result, we do think that the economy probably is going to be on a slower growth trajectory."
Canada's economic growth flat in July
On Tuesday, Statistics Canada reported that GDP for July was flat from the previous month.

"The goods-producing industries grouping was essentially unchanged in July, as increases in construction and utilities were offset by declines in the other sectors comprising the aggregate," the agency stated.
"The services-producing industries aggregate was essentially flat, as increases across several sectors were offset by declines in retail trade and wholesale trade."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Jeff Lagerquist is a senior writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Erin, Ont., he studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. Jeff previously worked as a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance Canada. He was also a reporter and digital producer for CTV National News, BNN Bloomberg and The Financial Post. He was also a Columbia University energy journalism fellow for 2025.

articles.title: Tulfo flags alleged favoritism in NHA's housing projects
articles.summary: Senator Raffy Tulfo on Tuesday flagged alleged "palakasan," or patronage in National Housing Authority (NHA) housing projects, particularly for calamity and tragedy victims.

blocks.text: Published September 29, 2026 8:29pm
Senator Raffy Tulfo on Tuesday flagged alleged "palakasan," or patronage in National Housing Authority (NHA) housing projects, particularly for calamity and tragedy victims.

During the Senate deliberations on the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development and its attached agencies’ proposed ₱5.498-billion budget for 2027, Tulfo said that he received complaints that some local officials favor people they knew for housing.

“Talamak daw ang palakasan. Karamihan daw sa nabibigyan ng pabahay eh mga taga-munisipyo o dabarkads ni chairman, etc. Ito mayroon akong feedback galing sa netizens, in fact, may mga nag-email sa tanggapan ko,” he said.

(Favoritism is allegedly rampant. Most of those being given housing are allegedly municipal employees or close friends of the barangay chairman, etc. I have feedback from netizens here; in fact, some have sent emails to my office.)
For its part, the NHA said that the beneficiaries of their housing project comes from the local government unit.
The agency also said that the only validation they conduct is by checking if those in the list have yet to receive a house.

“Mayroon pong resettlement, mayroon pong calamity. So bago kami mag-start, mayroon na po talagang listahan ng beneficiaries. Itong listahan na ito ay galing ng LGU. Vina-validate ng OCD yung biktima ng bagyo o trahedya. Tsaka pinapasa sa amin, so vinavalidate lang namin ito based sa hindi sila naulit, kumbaga hindi pa sila nabigyan ng bahay noon,” said NHA General Manager Joeben Tai.

(There is resettlement, and there is calamity housing. So before we start, there is already a list of beneficiaries. This list comes from the LGU. The OCD validates the victims of the typhoon or tragedy. Then it is passed to us, so we only validate it based on whether they are duplicates—meaning they haven't been given a house before.)
However, Tulfo noted that the NHA should still make sure that those in the list of beneficiaries have no connections to the local officials issuing them.
The senator said that even those who already have a home of their own or have cars are still getting free housing due to connections.

“You have to have a system para masiguro na itong mga LGU na nagbibigay sa inyo ng listahan ay hindi yung listahan nila na pabor sa kanilang mga followers, pabor sa kanilang mga nagka-campaign, pabor sa kanilang mga tauhan,” said Tulfo.
(You have to have a system to ensure that these LGUs giving you lists aren't providing lists that favor their followers, favor their campaign workers, or favor their staff.)
The NHA assured that it will strictly monitor the list of beneficiaries, warning that home ownership rights will be revoked if housing units are sold to non-beneficiaries.

“Ito po yung mga naibebentang unit kung saan binenta ng mga benepisyaryo yung kanilang mga unit sa P200,000, P300,000. Ayan din po chine-check namin, upang masiguro na benepisyaryo lang po ang nakatira,” said Tai.
(These are the sold units where beneficiaries sold them for ₱200,000 or ₱300,000. That is also what we check, to ensure that only beneficiaries are living there.)
“Lugi rin po yung nakabili kasi kina-cancel namin 'yan, at pinapaalis namin yung nakabili,” he added.
(The buyers also lose out because we cancel those rights, and we evict the buyer.) — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Officials investigate possible new ransom note in Nancy Guthrie case
articles.summary:
Local sheriff’s department announces new development related to disappearance of TV host’s mother in Arizona

Authorities are looking into the possibility of a new ransom note related to the…

blocks.text: Authorities are looking into the possibility of a new ransom note related to the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie, nearly eight months after she went missing from her Arizona home, the Pima county sheriff’s department said.

The sheriff’s department and the FBI Guthrie taskforce were recently made aware of the possible ransom note as well as social media comments related to it, the statement from the sheriff’s department said on Monday. Investigators are working to determine its credibility.
Officials did not immediately release details on how they found the note or what was in it.

In July, authorities released two ransom notes initially sent to a Tucson television station days after the mother of the Today show host Savannah Guthrie went missing on 1 February from her home outside Tucson.

The first note, sent on 2 February, said Nancy Guthrie was safe but scared and would be released unharmed once her captors received $4m in cryptocurrency. The second note, sent on 6 February, said Guthrie died shortly after she was kidnapped. Authorities have not said whether Guthrie is still alive.

No suspects have been arrested in her disappearance. The investigation is dogged by unanswered questions, such as how many people are believed to have taken part in her abduction and whether she was taken by someone who knew her.
The FBI had also released surveillance videos of a masked person who authorities said appeared to tamper with a camera on Nancy Guthrie’s front porch and block it with a plant.
Nancy Guthrie’s family has shared their pleas for information in videos posted to social media.

articles.title: Two US navy aviators eject while landing on carrier off Virginia
articles.summary:
Four sailors injured during unexplained ‘mishap’ onboard USS Dwight D Eisenhower aircraft carrier

Two US navy aviators ejected…

blocks.text: Two US navy aviators ejected as they were landing their plane on the USS Dwight D Eisenhower aircraft carrier off the coast of Virginia on Monday, and four sailors onboard the vessel were injured in what naval officials characterized as a “mishap”.

The two aviators, assigned to Carrier Air Wing 3, successfully ejected as “a mishap occurred during aircraft recovery operations” and were rescued by search and rescue personnel, the navy said in a short statement.

Both were returned to the ship and were being evaluated by medical personnel, the navy said. The four shipboard personnel also were receiving medical care, including one who was transported to a hospital in the Norfolk, Virginia, area for treatment of non-life-threatening injuries.

The navy did not say which type of two-seater plane was involved in the accident, nor what happened to the plane or what might have caused the accident. The navy did not immediately answer a request for further details.
The nuclear-powered Nimitz-class USS Dwight D Eisenhower was commissioned in 1977.

articles.title: Unmatched EJ Obiena shatters Asian Games record to defend throne
articles.summary: EJ Obiena delivers the Philippines' third gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games as he breaks his own record to repeat as men's pole vault champion

blocks.text: CHAMPION. Pole vaulter EJ Obiena in action for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
EJ Obiena delivers the Philippines' third gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games as he breaks his own record to repeat as men's pole vault champion
MANILA, Philippines – When it comes to Asia, EJ Obiena is in a league of his own.

And he reinforced that notion as Obiena defended his Asian Games crown following a record-breaking performance in men’s pole vault at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan on Tuesday, September 29.

Obiena set a new Asian Games mark after clearing 5.91 meters in a single attempt, delivering the Philippines’ third gold medal in this edition after gymnastics star Carlos Yulo won the first two in artistic gymnastics.
He shattered his own record of 5.90m, which Obiena set in 2023 when he won his first Asian Games title in Hangzhou, China.

After two failed attempts at 5.80m, Obiena upped the ante by going for 5.91m, which he surpassed with room to spare on the way to becoming the first back-to-back champion in the event since Kazakhstan’s Igor Potapovich won in 1994 and 1998.
It marked the first time Obiena cleared over 5.90m since he posted 5.97m in ruling the Irena Szewinska Memorial in 2024.
Two Chinese bets completed the podium, with Yao Jie and Li Chenyang bagging silver and bronze, respectively, with 5.70m clearances.

Obiena highlighted the Philippines’ best athletics showing in decades, with the country also bagging a pair of bronze courtesy of John Cabang Tolentino (men’s 110m hurdles) and Victoria Bossong (women’s 800m). – Rappler.com

articles.title: M&S links up with Sephora to lure younger shoppers
articles.summary:
Beauty specialist will open branded areas in 100 Marks & Spencer stores and will sell its products on chain’s website

Marks & Spencer is has signed a deal with Sephora to open areas…

blocks.text: Marks & Spencer is has signed a deal with Sephora to open areas under the beauty brand’s name within its stores, in its latest tactic to attract younger shoppers.
The French retailer is set to launch branded areas staffed by Sephora employees in 100 M&S stores and sell through the British retailer’s website in spring next year.

Seophora relaunched in the UK in 2023 with huge fanfare and now has about 18 stand-alone British stores. The company is owned by LVMH, the luxury goods group led by Bernard Arnault, who with his family is among the world’s richest people with a $171bn (£129bn) fortune, according to Forbes.

The company has rapidly expanded on its second attempt to enter the UK market after closing a handful of stores in 2005, having failed make a dent in a competitive sector. The deal with M&S marks a new strategy in its expansion plans.

Analysts have said Sephora’s work with up-and-coming brands and collaborations with high-profile influencers on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube has helped the brand reach its target female audience of 24- to 36-year-olds.

John Lyttle, the managing director of M&S’s fashion, home and beauty division, said: “Beauty is an important category for M&S, with the potential to attract new customers to shop with us and give existing customers the opportunity to shop with us more often.”

“Combining Sephora’s specialist expertise with the strength of the M&S brand, our store estate and our growing digital platform,” Lyttle said. “Alongside this, we will continue investing in our own-label beauty categories where we have established strength and customer trust.”

blocks.caption: A jointly branded Marks & Spencer and Sephora shopping bag. Photograph: Marks & Spencer/PA

blocks.text: Retailers have been battling to grab a share of the beauty market after the disappearance of many department stores. In recent years a swathe of UK department stores have closed, including Debenhams, Beales and about half the House of Fraser chain.

Sephora’s self-service model – which allows consumers to touch and test makeup and perfume without the help of shop staff – is seen to appeal to younger shoppers, who may test in store and buy online. The tie-up could provide increased competition for the specialist health and beauty chains Boots and Superdrug.

Lyttle said the deal was part of M&S’s wider transformation plan, which involves £700m of investments in revitalising stores, modernising its supply chain and distribution system, and further improvements in products.
after newsletter promotion

The group, which employs more than 65,000 people, has 227 full-line stores – containing food, clothing, homewares and beauty – after closing dozens of old and out-of-place outlets. More will shut over the next two years and a handful of new outlets are opening with the aim to have 200 full-line stores in the UK.

M&S’s food arm is expanding rapidly, with 18 food-only stores opening this year as it heads for a target of 420, compared with 335 directly operated outlets. Franchise partners run another 466 in the UK and more overseas.

Sarah Boyd, the managing director of Sephora UK, said: “Together, we can redefine what high street beauty means for customers across the UK, bringing the very best curated brand and beauty experience to the M&S stores.”

She said the group would introduce its beauty advisers to M&S stores to “provide a truly personalised experience, and to reach customers in more communities where they already live, shop and spend their time”.

articles.title: Spain announces new housing measures after protests over 87-year-old woman's eviction
articles.summary: The measures include a proposed ban on evictions until 2030 and the automatic renewal of tenant contracts.

blocks.text: Spain's coalition government has approved new housing measures following protests over the country's housing crisis, sparked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home in Madrid last week.
Ministers met on Tuesday to discuss the proposals, which include a potential ban on evictions until 2030, Health Minister Mónica García said.
She said the measures would bring relief to more than five million people - but opposition politician Míriam Nogueras said the agreement left "small landlords out in the cold".
The new housing measures need to be approved in parliament, where the leftist coalition government lacks a majority.

García said other measures agreed upon on Tuesday included the rolling over of contracts until 2028; stricter regulation of short-term and room rentals; and banning the the purchase of housing by investment firms.
"It is time to intervene in the speculative housing market and start striking a balance between ordinary citizens and vulture funds," García said.
Referencing the protests, she added: "Thanks to the mobilisations and the encampments. Without you, this would not have been possible."

But Nogueras, spokeswoman for the pro-Catalan independence party Junts, said: "We all agreed that evictions - where the property is owned by a fund, a vulture fund, run by someone managing millions of euros - obviously need to be stopped."

"Lumping together in this category those who have invested their savings in a flat, a restaurant or a property - putting them all in the same basket - is a mistake," she told Spanish public broadcaster RTVE.
The minority government, which is made up of the ruling Socialists and the junior partners Sumar, has 30 days from the decree's publication to reach an agreement in parliament.
Socialist Housing Minister Isabel Rodríguez is set to give further details on the measures at a news conference later on Tuesday.

articles.title: Solons hit China: We don't need your nod to operate over WPS
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Lawmakers from the House of Representatives’ Young Guns bloc have questioned China’s latest interference during a rotation and resupply (RoRe) mission to Ayungin Shoal, saying…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Lawmakers from the House of Representatives’ Young Guns bloc have questioned China’s latest interference during a rotation and resupply (RoRe) mission to Ayungin Shoal, saying that local authorities do not need to seek permission to operate in an area that belongs to the Philippines.

In a joint statement, the House Young Guns said that Filipino troops do not have to seek permission from China as they are moving within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone (EEZ) — since Ayungin or the Second Thomas Shoal is well within the country’s 370-kilometer EEZ.
The statement was issued by Deputy Speakers Paolo Ortega V and Jefferson Khonghun, along with Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong and Manila Rep. Ernix Dionisio.
“What is this now? Only you believe what you are saying. We do not need your permission,” the lawmakers said.

“Our personnel were delivering sustainment and rotating Filipinos stationed on a commissioned Philippine naval vessel inside our exclusive economic zone. That is a sovereign duty. It does not require Beijing’s permission,” they added.

The Young Guns bloc was referring to the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) decision to suspend their RoRe mission to Ayungin Shoal last Sept. 24, after Chinese coast guard and naval vessels interfered with the Philippine convoy.
The mission was meant to deliver supplies and rotate personnel stationed aboard the BRP Sierra Madre, which was deliberately beached at Ayungin, and is now acting as an outpost at the region.

AFP spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea (WPS) Rear Adm. Roy Vincent Trinidad said on Friday that three People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) warships and five China Coast Guard (CCG) vessels interfered with the routine mission.
The M/V Lapu-Lapu and three Philippine Navy and Philippine Coast Guard support vessels were still about 111 kilometers from Ayungin Shoal when they were hindered by the Chinese vessels.

According to Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea (WPS) Rear Adm. Jay Tarriela, China was asserting its position in the WPS after the latest interference of Chinese coast guard and naval vessels against a Philippine convoy.
But the lawmakers believe that even if China calls the activity as mere monitoring, it is not lawful since the area is within the Philippines’ EEZ.
“Calling that ‘monitoring’ does not make it lawful,” the Young Guns lawmakers said.
They also urged authorities to continue doing the mission, as local and international laws have declared that the WPS belongs to the Philippines.

“Continue the missions. Record every hazardous encounter,” they said. “The West Philippine Sea is ours under the Constitution, (the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea or) Unclos, and a binding award. We will not leave our troops unsupported.”

Last Sunday, the United States (US) condemned China’s interference, with US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton saying that the CCG and the PLAN made “irresponsible maneuvers” that threatened a collision with a Philippine vessel and prevented a lawful and routine resupply mission to the shoal.
“We stand by our Philippine allies and laud their professionalism and restraint,” Lipton said.
“We call on the China Coast Guard and PLAN to cease the use of escalatory tactics that threaten the freedom of navigation and a free and open Indo-Pacific,” he added.

This is not the first time that CCG vessels tried to drive away local authorities from carrying out Rore missions. Just this July, the AFP reported that a Navy personnel was injured after members of the CCG assaulted him during a confrontation at Ayungin Shoal.

AFP said that a CCG rigid hull inflatable boat (RHIB) with eight personnel, coming from vessel CCGV 21560, unlawfully approached within close range of the BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin. It circled and took photos and videos, prompting two AFP rubber boats “to calmly and non‑confrontationally drive it away.”

However, the military said the situation escalated when CCG personnel “reacted violently and aggressively” by striking a Philippine Navy personnel on the head with a wooden baton, causing an injury and damaging the Navy rubber boat.

The WPS, a body of water that forms part of the South China Sea, is inside the western side of the Philippines’ EEZ. China however has insisted ownership on many islands inside the WPS, despite the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) award in 2016 which stated that the Philippines has exclusive rights over its waters.

Incidents between the two countries over this area have occurred several times, and are well-documented. In August 2023, a CCG vessel water-cannoned Philippine vessels which were only trying to bring supplies to soldiers at BRP Sierra Madre.

In response to the event, China claimed that a former administration promised to remove BRP Sierra Madre from Ayungin, but the promise has not been acted upon. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. then said that he has not made that agreement, and if such a deal exists, it has already been terminated. /das

articles.title: COA finds ‘unverifiable’ beneficiaries in DepEd’s SHS voucher program
articles.summary: The dozens of unverifiable beneficiaries of the senior high school voucher program resulted in an overpayment of P938,000, according to state auditors

blocks.text: DEPED. The Department of Education headquarters in Pasig City.
Angie de Silva/Rappler
The dozens of unverifiable beneficiaries of the senior high school voucher program resulted in an overpayment of P938,000, according to state auditors

items: The Commission on Audit identified 58 unverifiable beneficiaries of the Department of Education's senior high school voucher program, leading to an overpayment of P938,000 for the school year 2025-2026.

The unverifiable beneficiaries included students who dropped out, transferred, were not enrolled, deceased, or absent during validation, highlighting deficiencies in beneficiary validation and monitoring by the DepEd.
In response to the findings, the DepEd has tightened its validation and accountability measures and has begun recovering overpayments.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – There were 58 “unverifiable” beneficiaries of the Department of Education‘s (DepEd) senior high school (SHS) voucher program, which resulted in an overpayment of P938,000 in school year (SY) 2025-2026, the Commission on Audit (COA) found.
According to COA’s compliance audit on the existence and eligibility of voucher beneficiaries, the flagged unvalidated beneficiaries were:

items: 32 students who had officially or unofficially dropped out
12 who transferred to other schools
11 who were not enrolled in the second semester
2 who were reported deceased
1 who was absent during validation with no records available

blocks.text: The overpayment of P938,000, which was for 53 out of the 58 unverified beneficiaries, had already been released to their respective schools, COA said in its 2025 annual audit report on the DepEd released last September 23.
Four beneficiaries were excluded from billing statements prior to payment as of February, while the subsidy for one beneficiary had not yet been released as of March.
Moreover, state auditors found five beneficiaries who were “misclassified under incorrect voucher categories,” resulting in an overpayment of P14,710.

Other deficiencies seen were incomplete or improperly maintained supporting documents and inadequate monitoring by the DepEd and the Private Education Assistance Committee, which helps in implementing the Government Assistance to Students and Teachers in Private Education (GATSPE).

“These lapses expose the program to the risk of erroneous billing and overpayment, compromise the reliability of beneficiary validation, and may result in the disbursement of funds to ineligible beneficiaries, contrary to the objective of providing financial assistance exclusively to qualified learners,” COA said.

The SHS voucher program is a government financial subsidy program for qualified Grades 11 and 12 students. It provides assistance in the form of vouchers ranging from P14,000 to P22,500 per year, which are paid directly to the student’s chosen private school.
COA said the program’s participating schools are responsible for encoding and updating student information.
“The status of the concerned [voucher program beneficiaries] should have been duly updated and subjected to DepEd verification to prevent potential overpayments,” the commission added.
On Tuesday, September 29, the DepEd said it had acted on the COA findings.

“As part of its five-layer validation, DepEd, through its co-manager of the senior high school voucher program, Private Education Assistance Committee, has completed its school year 2025-2026 validation. Through this year-end validation, flagged cases are being reviewed and confirmed overpayments will be recovered,” part of the DepEd’s statement read.
The agency said it had “tightened beneficiary validation, billing, refund, and accountability measures” in the revised Expanded GATSPE guidelines released in April.
The DepEd said it will “continue to pursue accountability and the recovery of government funds where warranted.”
The DepEd investigated 12 private schools in February 2025 over the alleged presence of ghost students in the SHS voucher program.
By March 2025, the agency recovered P65 million from the voucher program amid irregularities, with 38 private schools fully refunding the government.

In July 2026, the DepEd said a regional trial court had sentenced an individual to up to 14 years in prison for attempting to defraud the government program by submitting falsified documents. Case details were not provided.
In the same 2025 annual audit report, COA also flagged deficiencies in monitoring the implementation of the SHS voucher program.
As of October 2025, there were 172,909 billed beneficiaries in participating private senior high schools nationwide, excluding the Bangsamoro region and the Negros Island Region, according to COA.

State auditors found the unverifiable beneficiaries from a sample population of 5,507 in SY 2025-2026. Of the number, 995 beneficiaries came from the National Capital Region, while the rest were from other regions, covering 571 senior high schools participating in the voucher program. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Two former Hungarian ministers detained over suspected bribery and misuse of public funds
articles.summary:
Ministers from Viktor Orbán’s former far-right government arrested after MPs vote to lift their immunity

Two ministers in Viktor Orbán’s former far-right government suspected separately of…

blocks.text: Two ministers in Viktor Orbán’s former far-right government suspected separately of misusing millions of euros of public funds and taking millions more in bribes have been detained, hours after Hungarian MPs voted to lift their immunity.

Prosecutors said on Tuesday that Balázs Hankó, Orbán’s culture minister and still an MP in the former prime minister’s nationalist Fidesz party, was ​taken into custody late on Monday. Hankó is suspected of misappropriation of funds. He has denied any wrongdoing.

Miklós Seszták, an MP from Fidesz ally KDNP who served as minister for national development between 2014 and 2018, was also detained on Monday as part of an ⁠investigation into alleged bribery. He too has denied wrongdoing.

“Yesterday was an important day,” said Hungary’s prime minister, Péter Magyar on Tuesday. His Tisza party swept to victory in April elections promising to investigate alleged corruption and abuse of office during Orbán’s 16-year rule.

“After decades of lies, for the first time, many millions of Hungarians could experience what real regime change and equality before the law really mean, Magyar said on social media. “Hungary is no longer a country without consequences.”

The arrests came hours after Hungary’s parliament on Monday voted to suspend Hankó and Seszták’s immunity – but also that of Magyar, who had asked for his to be lifted so he could clear himself of what he called a “character assassination”.

The graft investigations into the Orbán-era ministers are the first against senior figures in the former government. Magyar, meanwhile, is accused of snatching a phone from a man filming him in a nightclub in 2024 and throwing it into the Danube River.

The prime minister has denied his conduct amounted to theft and called the case, which involves a damages claim of €300 (£260), a “sham”. He said he took responsibility for his actions but denied committing a crime and criticised prosecutors for “conflating” the ex-ministers’ corruption cases with “an attempted political character assassination”.

Magyar ​has repeatedly said that in recent years corruption and misuse of public funds have cost Hungary between 8% and 10% of its GDP under successive governments led by Orbán, who has repeatedly denied allowing rampant corruption and outright theft of public money during more than a decade and half in power.

Prosecutors allege Hankó oversaw the criminal misuse of 17.3bn forints (€47m) of public funds from Hungary’s national cultural fund (NKA), channelling the money to artists and groups with ties to Fidesz and financing its 2026 election campaign.
“My conscience is clear, this is a political show trial,” Hankó said ‌in a live video broadcast on Orbán’s Facebook page shortly before his arrest.

In July, police raided the Fidesz offices and seized the party’s internet servers in connection ⁠with alleged “misappropriation and other criminal offences” at the NKA, prompting Orbán to accuse authorities of conducting a sham investigation in order to render his party “legally unviable”.

Prosecutors also suspect Seszták of accepting more than 12bn forints (€32.6m) in bribes and kickbacks connected to vehicle procurements under Hungary’s state bus company, as well as to public construction projects. The case centres on the purchase of secondhand buses at allegedly inflated prices.

Separately, Hungary’s national ‌asset protection and recovery office, the anti-corruption body established by Magyar’s government as part of his anti-graft ⁠drive, on ⁠Monday announced the ​first four cases it intends to tackle.

The first concerned “selling ​political connections to obtain residence permits ‌for employment”, the body said in a statement, and the second case is about alleged corruption involving local council expenditure on park maintenance and public catering.
The third case involved “a state-owned company and state investments” and has links to Dániel Jellinek, a real estate mogul and one of Hungary’s wealthiest businessmen, the statement said.

The real estate firm that Jellinek heads has said he will cooperate fully with the authorities. “Our firm position is that Mr Jellinek has not committed any offence in connection with the matter. We are confident that the investigation will confirm this and that the proceedings against him will soon be discontinued,” it said in a statement this month.

The fourth concerned “seemingly unjustified propaganda ​and event costs” at the sovereignty protection office, ​an Orbán-era body set up to monitor what Fidesz alleged was “undue political interference” by foreign entities in Hungary, and abolished by Magyar’s government in June.

articles.title: Poa denies agreeing with Panelo over 'lokohan' remark
articles.summary: Lawyer Michael Poa, spokesperson for Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team, on Tuesday denied agreeing with Duterte's spokesperson Paolo Panelo, who described as a joke the Senate impeachment…

blocks.text: SARA DUTERTE IMPEACHMENT TRIAL
Published September 29, 2026 8:05pm

Lawyer Michael Wesley Poa, spokesperson for Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team, on Tuesday denied agreeing with Duterte's spokesperson Paolo Panelo, who described as a joke the Senate impeachment court's ruling on the basis for determining the voting threshold for her conviction.
Poa was referring to Panelo's remarks to reporters on September 23, when the latter said the impeachment court's ruling was a "joke" and claimed that Poa shared his sentiments.
"That's not true. Actually, just to set the record straight, I didn't agree with him on anything as to lokohan (a joke) or anything like that," Poa said in a press briefing.
"I always maintained candor with all of you. I always maintained respect to the court," he added.
Poa said any disagreement with the court's decision should be addressed through the proper legal process, not through media interviews or informal discussions.
Senator-judges voted 13-1-6 to set the conviction threshold at two-thirds of those legally allowed to participate in the proceedings.
This means Duterte could be convicted with fewer than 16 votes, as several senators are facing charges, remain in hiding or are on medical leave.
The defense team is considering appealing the Senate impeachment court's ruling before the Supreme Court.
After the impeachment court issued its ruling last week, Panelo said he and Poa believed the decision was a "joke."

Panelo told reporters: "Nung nag-usap naman kami kanina parang agree kami doon sa nangyari na lokohan lang 'to, lokohan na itong nangyayari. Kaya posible silang umakyat sa Korte Suprema. Pero hindi ko narinig actually kung ano sinabi niya sa press briefing."

(When we talked to each other earlier, it seemed like we agreed that what happened was just a farce, that what is happening is a joke. That's why it's possible they'll elevate it to the Supreme Court. But I actually didn't hear what he said at the press briefing.)
For his part, Poa said he had already messaged Panelo about the statement and asked him why he had made such remarks.

“I messaged him personally and basically asked him why he said that. Well, I will just leave it at that. He is the spokesperson of the vice president, but I will not allow my name to be dragged into something that I had nothing to do with,” Poa said.
"He assured me that it won't happen again," he added.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Spain agrees on measures to fix housing crisis, ban eviction
articles.summary: Spain's cabinet ministers said they have consensus on new measures to curb the housing crisis in the country after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen last week from her apartment sparked protests.

image.caption: Maricarmen was evicted last week from her apartment, sparking nationwide protests that place the housing crisis in the spotlightImage: David Canales/SOPA Images/IMAGO

blocks.text: Spain's coalition government on Tuesday said it has agreed new measures to tackle the country's housing crisis after the forceful removal of an 87-year-old pensioner from her apartment in Madrid last week, sparked nationwide solidarity protests.
Spanish Health Minister Monica Garcia said the housing legislation includes a ban on evictions until 2030, tighter rules for short-term rentals and a two-year extension for existing leases.

"It's ‌time ​to intervene in the speculative housing market and ​begin to rebalance the scales between ⁠citizens ​and vulture funds," ​Garcia, who belongs ​to the ‌leftist government's junior coalition partner Sumar, ​wrote ⁠in a post on ⁠X.
Legislation still needs to pass through parliament
The Spanish government, led byPrime Minister Pedro Sanchez and his ministers, approved the measures after a meeting.
But since Sanchez leads a minority government, he is still dependent on votes from a number of other parties in parliament before the bill is set in law.
Sanchez's ruling Socialists were engaged in talks with coalition partners Sumar and others up to Tuesday.
Socialist Housing Minister Isabel Rodriguez is scheduled to address a press conference later on Tuesday.
A case that triggered mass protests in Spain

Images and videos last week that showed Maria del Carmen Abascal — known by her nickname Maricarmen — escorted out of her apartment by riot police officers touched a nerve among Spaniards who've long called for a solution to the housing crisis in the country.
Maricarmen's father had first rented the property in 1956 in Madrid's Retiro neighborhood and she continued as the tenant after her parents died.
Spanish newspaper El Pais reported that Maricarmen had rented the apartment from a private landlord until 2018, after which a real estate company acquired the property and took over its management.

blocks.caption: Thousands demonstrate against evictions and the housing crisis in Spain Image: Richard Zubelzu/NurPhoto/picture alliance
Demonstrators set up camps at Puerta del Sol squareImage: David Canales/SOPA Images/Sipa USA/picture alliance
Protesters were angry that Maricarmen was removed from the apartment she lived in since 1956Image: Bruno Thevenin/Middle East Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: According to the newspaper, the legal dispute between Maricarmen and the real estate company lasted eight years and their latest attempt to evict her from the apartment marked their fourth attempt to do so.

The issue placed Spain's housing market in the spotlight where many long-term tenants have been priced out of their apartments due to an affordability crisis and a shortage of homes in Europe's fourth-largest economy.
Protesters rallied around Maricarmen's cause, especially because pictures of her being taken out of her apartment building and into an ambulance were vividly present across social media.
She is a wheelchair user too.
People then hit the streets of Madrid in the thousands on Saturday, with many having ended their protest by setting up tents in Madrid's historic Puerta del Sol plaza at the end of the night.
More people, including multigenerational families, joined Sunday.
Maricarmen to return home because of 'social mobilization,' lawyer says
Maricarmen's lawyer on Monday said that she was going to be able to return home, calling the victory a "result of the social mobilization."
"If this agreement we have reached is signed, it will obviously be a better and happier outcome for everyone," Abascal's lawyer Beatriz Duro told reporters.

"Hopefully this agreement, this different way of ending this type of situation, which is unfortunately experienced every day in this country, helps to change the paradigm when it comes to housing in general," Duro said.

articles.title: ‘It takes a lot of work’: Deb Haaland puts addiction struggles at center of New Mexico governor bid
articles.summary:
First Native American woman to serve as US cabinet secretary candid about history with alcohol as she seeks to tackle billowing public health crisis

“It clouds your mind,” recalls

blocks.text: “It clouds your mind,” recalls Deb Haaland, the trailblazing US cabinet secretary now running to be New Mexico’s next governor. “They say that, after the first drink, you lose your judgment.”

Haaland developed a drinking problem after leaving high school and was twice arrested for driving under the influence. But in her 20s she decided to get sober, a battle that required personal commitment and critical external support. She went on to become a member of Congress, one of the first two Native American women ever elected to the House, and then to become the first Native American to serve as a US cabinet secretary.

Now Haaland is writing her next chapter. The Democrat is taking the unusual step of putting her own 35 years of sobriety and her past struggles with alcoholism at the center of her campaign for governor in November’s midterm elections.

In a statewide six-figure broadcast and digital ad buy launching ahead of the election, Haaland links her intimate experience with addiction directly to the public health crisis ravaging local communities.

“I guess I’m like so many New Mexicans,” she told the Guardian by phone on Monday. “I started abusing alcohol at a young age and I was very fortunate that, at the age of 23, I recognised that I wanted to live a sober life and so I went on that journey and worked on myself for quite a while. It’s a lot of hard work to pay attention to yourself. I recognised there were so many things in my life that I needed to change.”

She added: “I was fortunate to have the help of an inpatient treatment programme way back then, and so that helped me to get sober initially, but it takes a lot of work even after your head clears. I went to meetings and therapy and all of those things. I found the help that I needed and thankfully I’ve been sober for 35 years now.”

Haaland, a member of the Pueblo of Laguna tribe who grew up in a military family, served in Congress from 2019 to 2021 then as interior secretary in Joe Biden’s cabinet from 2021 to 2025. She is now taking on Republican Gregg Hull, the former mayor of Rio Rancho, in the election for governor of New Mexico.

In a political era in which personal vulnerability is often weaponised, her campaign is betting that voters in The Land of Enchantment – where the deadly fentanyl crisis has touched families in every corner of the state – will appreciate her candid treatment of a subject once regarded as taboo.

“I look at this as a public health issue,” she emphasised. “I look at this as not somebody with a moral failing but essentially a victim of this terrible disease. We want to make sure that this is looked at as a public health issue, that we move some behavioural health dollars to this area so that people can get the help they need.”

She notes that the pervasive stigma surrounding substance use disorder frequently prevents families from seeking life-saving care. “For a lot of folks it’s hard not to feel remorse and shame and all of those things,” Haaland said.

But attitudes are changing. “This fentanyl crisis in our state affects even our smallest rural communities here in New Mexico. It’s hitting us in the face. People are dying from this drug, and so I feel like any shame or remorse that anyone might feel about a family member in facing this type of substance use disorder, we would put that aside and say we want people to find the help they need.”

The campaign’s political ad brings these human stories into sharp focus. The spot features Jorge, a local father who announces on screen: “I am one year and one month sober.” Jorge tells viewers that while addiction leaves individuals feeling isolated, “there’s a community of people that understand completely.”

The commercial also features David, a behavioural health psychologist, who highlights Haaland’s plan to force insurance providers to cover comprehensive treatment and crack down on drug-trafficking networks. Jorge closes: “With Deb, I have hope.”

blocks.caption: Deb Haaland with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez as congresswomen-elect in November 2018. Photograph: Mandel Ngan/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Haaland frames her recovery experience as the foundation for reforming New Mexico’s fractured health infrastructure. She offers sharp criticism of former Republican governor Susana Martinez, whose administration dismantled local treatment networks through unproven fraud allegations against providers.

Haaland said: “She essentially destroyed our behavioural health system. She accused a lot of behavioural health professionals of fraud and so many of them went out of business and it took years for the attorney general to clear them all of any wrongdoing. It’s easy to demolish something; it’s difficult to build something back, so we’re still building back from that and I feel committed to helping people live better lives.”

She proposes a structural redesign to prevent addiction being funneled into the criminal justice system. Haaland proposes creating a state office of community safety that would deploy behavioural health specialists to non-criminal emergency calls on street corners, allowing police officers to focus their resources on violent crime and drug traffickers.

“A lot of these issues with substance use are not criminal in nature and so my office of community safety would ensure that we can help law enforcement to focus on crime. Drug traffickers are part of crime and then we can focus on the people who are suffering.”

Haaland’s campaign trail stops have included visits to extended residential care facilities such as Grand Summit, in Albuquerque, which provides long-term housing, job assistance and financial support for recovering residents.

During a recent stop, Haaland invited programme residents to walk across the street and cast their ballots alongside her. “They felt empowered and they felt like they were part of something larger than themselves,” she reflected.

Haaland’s focus on community health coincides with looming federal challenges. She raised alarm over impending Medicaid rollbacks under the Trump administration, scheduled to begin on 1 January, that could strip addiction treatment coverage from vulnerable state residents. In response, New Mexico has established a Medicaid trust fund intended to provide longer-term support for the programme.

She also voiced opposition to aggressive federal enforcement actions in New Mexico, calling recent ICE raids “untenable” “cruel” and “ruthless”, referencing an incident where an individual was detained in front of his 11-year-old child outside a medical clinic. “They wear masks, they don’t identify themselves.”
Haaland also linked voter discontent to economic pressures such as tariffs and rising fuel costs, which hit rural New Mexicans commuting up to 100 miles round-trip for work.
“I can’t say why people are coming out to vote and why people want to build this momentum in New Mexico for Democrats,” she said, “but it’s happening.”

articles.title: Albania: As corruption cases multiply, experts question whether the anti-corruption drive is addressing the causes or just the symptoms
articles.summary: From a former president to the ex-intelligence chief, Albania is prosecuting senior officials at a rate once thought impossible. But do more prosecutions mean less corruption or simply better…

image.caption: Vlora Hyseni, former head of Albania's State Intelligence Service, leaves the offices of Albania's Special Prosecution Office against Corruption and Organized Crime (SPAK), where she answered questions about her alleged involvement in a major corruption scandalImage: Armando Babani/Matrix Images/pic

blocks.text: On September 22, the head of Albania's State Intelligence Service, Vlora Hyseni, was in Baku, Azerbaijan, attending an international conference of intelligence service chiefs. Back in Tirana, the Special Court had ordered her house arrest over two suspected criminal offences: supporting the perpetrator of a crime and disclosure of investigative secrecy.

The investigation into Hyseni emerged from a wider corruption case involving the National Agency for Information Society (AKSHI), the agency responsible for much of Albania's digital public infrastructure.
Prosecutors suspect that she used information available to her as intelligence chief to help a person wanted in that investigation.
Hyseni turned herself in to the Albanian authorities later that day and remains under house arrest as the investigation continues. She has since been dismissed as head of the intelligence service.
Rise in criminal proceedings and investigations
Hyseni's case is the latest in a series of criminal proceedings that have reached unusually high into Albania's political and state establishment.

blocks.caption: Political scientist Afrim Krasniqi says that after the 2016 reform, Albania's new justice institutions were expected to 'focus on high-level corruption and "VIP" cases'Image: Afrim Krasniqi/Privatarchiv

blocks.text: A former president has spent almost two years in detention, a former prime minister is on trial, the mayor of Tirana has been behind bars since early 2025, two former deputy prime ministers under Prime Minister Edi Rama have also faced criminal proceedings, and investigations have been launched into senior officials in agencies controlling large areas of public spending and state infrastructure.
These are all separate cases, but they all involve alleged abuse of public power.
How did Albania get here?
For years, the problem was completely the opposite: High-level corruption in Albania was widely associated with impunity.
This is why bringing senior political figures accused of wrongdoing before the courts became one of the central expectations of the justice reform launched in 2016.

"The expectation was that the new justice institutions would focus on high-level corruption and 'VIP' cases," says Afrim Krasniqi, a political scientist and executive director of the Institute for Political Studies in Tirana. "There were individuals who stood above the law, and impunity was pronounced," he told DW.

blocks.caption: Dorian Matlija says that Albania is 'becoming more effective at punishing corruption after it has occurred, but much less capable of preventing it'Image: Kristi Çavo

blocks.text: The reform fundamentally reshaped Albania's justice system and created new institutions to investigate corruption and organized crime, including the Special Anti-Corruption Structure, SPAK.
But the change was not immediate. Building the new institutions took years, and older cases were often more difficult to investigate.

For Dorian Matlija, a lawyer and executive director of Albanian civil society organization Res Publica, the number of senior officials now facing criminal proceedings does not necessarily mean that corruption is more widespread today than it was in the past.

"What has changed significantly is the institutional reaction," Matlija told DW. "Today, SPAK is a specialized structure with greater independence, stronger capacities and international support, as well as the willingness to undertake investigations that have broken the myth of the untouchability of senior officials."
The other side of accountability
But bringing senior officials before the courts is only one measure of whether institutions are working.

blocks.caption: Albania applied for EU membership in 2009 and was granted candidate status in June 2014. Pictured here: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama and President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen (both center)Image: Valdrin Xhemaj/REUTERS

blocks.text: By the time a corruption case reaches prosecutors, the alleged abuse has already taken place. For Matlija, this is where Albania's progress is far less clear.
"We are becoming more effective at punishing corruption after it has occurred, but much less capable of preventing it," he said.

Matlija points to the institutions and mechanisms that are supposed to act before a case becomes criminal: administrative controls, audits, conflict-of-interest rules and asset declarations. In his assessment, these have often proved ineffective.

The European Commission's 2025 report on Albania reaches a similar conclusion. It said that SPAK has made "tangible progress towards a solid track record in the fight against corruption." At the same time, the report says that corruption remains widespread and that "the institutional framework for prevention of corruption continued to have a limited impact."
The impact on citizens
The problem is also visible in citizens' encounters with public officials.

In a 2023 survey by the anti-corruption and good governance coalition SELDI (Southeast Europe Leadership for Development and Integrity), 52% of respondents in Albania said they had experienced corruption pressure from public officials, while 40% reported having paid a bribe.

Krasniqi sees the problem in broader political terms. Albania has been governed by Rama's Socialist Party since 2013, and the party currently holds an outright majority in parliament. He argues that this prolonged political dominance has weakened the checks and balances that should constrain the executive.
"We have a deformed system," he said. "The head of the executive controls the executive, parliament and institutions."

He argues that this concentration of power has been accompanied by informal networks of influence, with people outside state institutions able to shape political decisions, legislation and the use of public assets.
Rama has repeatedly maintained that criminal responsibility is individual when investigations have reached senior officials. Responding to the Hyseni case, he returned to the same position.
"When a senior official has opened an account with justice, the case of the former intelligence chief is an individual matter between her and the justice system," Rama said.
What does this mean for Albania's EU accession hopes?

In May, the EU confirmed that the country had met the interim benchmarks for the "fundamentals" cluster, which includes the rule of law, and moved into a phase focused on implementation and lasting results.
Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index shows Albania improving from 33 points in 2012 to 39 in 2025 but still ranking below all EU member states.
For Matlija, Albania's efforts to advance EU integration helped create the conditions that allowed institutions such as SPAK to become stronger and more independent.

"The EU no longer demands only the adoption of laws and reforms, but also concrete and sustainable results. This creates constant pressure for justice institutions to be genuinely effective and independent of political power," he said.

For Krasniqi, this is also where the meaning of European integration lies. Membership, he argues, should not be judged only by Albania's progress through the formal accession process, but by whether the country itself changes.

"The essence should be for Albania, Albanian society and Albanian institutions to change and improve, so that we become worthy of integration," he said. For him, that change should also be felt by citizens through greater social security, prosperity and independence, rather than being just a series of formal achievements.

articles.title: Victoria Bossong claims 800m bronze in Asian Games debut
articles.summary: The fastest in the heats, Victoria Bossong finishes third in the women's 800 final as she delivers the Philippines' second athletics medal in the 2026 Asian Games

blocks.text: REPRESENT. Athletics standout Victoria Bossong in action for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
The fastest in the heats, Victoria Bossong finishes third in the women's 800 final as she delivers the Philippines' second athletics medal in the 2026 Asian Games

MANILA, Philippines – Victoria Bossong turned in a slower time in the final but still salvaged an athletics medal for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games as she snagged the bronze in the women’s 800m at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan on Tuesday, September 29.

The Filipina-American middle-distance specialist clocked 2 minutes and 5.34 seconds to finish third and deliver the Philippines’ second athletics medal in this edition of the quadrennial showpiece after John Cabang Tolentino bagged bronze in the men’s 110m hurdles.
China’s Wu Hongjiao struck gold with 2:04.49, while Bahrain’s Nelly Korir clinched silver with 2:05.16 — the three medalists separated only by less than a second.
Bossong, whose mother, Catalina Atienza, hails from Oriental Mindoro, emerged as the title favorite after posting the fastest time in the heats, where she registered 2:02.34.

A repeat of that time would have netted the 23-year-old Harvard University graduate the Philippines’ first Asian Games gold medal in a track event since the late Lydia de Vega ruled the women’s 100m in the 1986 edition.
But it simply was not meant to be for Bossong, who owns a personal best of 1:58.52 — a time that eclipses the Asian Games record of 1:59.02 set by Kazakhstan’s Margarita Mukasheva in 2014.
Still, Bossong enjoyed a promising debut for the Philippines in a multi-sport event, which came just months after she gained eligibility in July to represent the country. – Rappler.com

articles.title: DND seeks NBI probe into fake Teodoro letter on Ayungin Shoal
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of National Defense (DND) has referred to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) a fake letter purportedly signed by Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of National Defense (DND) has referred to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) a fake letter purportedly signed by Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. concerning an operation at Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal, saying its circulation was part of a foreign interference campaign aimed at discrediting the Philippine government.
DND spokesperson Assistant Secretary Arsenio Andolong said on Tuesday that the letter, supposedly addressed to a certain Peter Enzminger, was fabricated.
“The Department unequivocally states that the document and its content are obviously and absolutely false and fake,” Andolong said in a statement.

“This is yet another episode of foreign interference and malign influence that is intended to discredit the legitimate and lawful efforts of the Philippine government to assert its national sovereignty and territorial integrity,” he added.

The two-page letter, which bore what appeared to be Teodoro’s signature, claimed that the defense chief had approved an operation at Ayungin Shoal on July 20 intended to expose Chinese actions ahead of the 59th Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.

It also contained claims about Philippine domestic politics and the country’s alliance with the United States, including a purported commitment by Teodoro to maintain support for the alliance regardless of changes in the domestic political climate.
The DND did not identify who was behind the letter’s circulation or provide evidence linking it to a foreign entity.
On July 20, two Philippine Navy personnel were injured during a confrontation with the China Coast Guard (CCG) near the grounded BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin Shoal.
CCG personnel struck a Filipino serviceman on the head with a wooden baton during the confrontation.

The Philippine Coast Guard evacuated the two injured personnel the following day despite what it described as blocking maneuvers by Chinese vessels. One serviceman sustained a head injury and arm bruising, while the other suffered a cut to an index finger that weakened his grip.

The incident prompted President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to summon Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to Malacañang, while Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro raised the Philippines’ protest with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on the sidelines of the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Manila.
Beijing denied the Philippine military’s account and blamed Filipino personnel for provoking the confrontation. /mcm
